title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In this 'quatrième mouture' of Analysis situs, Grothendieck works with an abstract combinatorial structure called a 'magasin' M. It carries an order-type relation ≤ (Y ≤ X reads roughly 'Y lies in the closure of X', a face/incidence relation) and a containment relation ≪. It also carries two disjointness relations: |∘| (separation, 'disjoint') and ∥ (a stronger disjointness). The 'figures' 𝓕 are certain down-closed subsets of M. The page begins item 1 of the programme announced on the previous page: axioms for the 'lieux'.

Step 1: the lieux.
- L ⊂ M is the set of elements that are minimal for ≪. These are the 'points'.
- For x, y ∈ L, Grothendieck states it is tautological that x ∥ y ⇔ x |∘| y. Points have no proper parts, so the two disjointness notions coincide on them.

Step 2: shadows and open shadows.
- The shadow ('ombre') of X is omb(X) = {x ∈ L | x ≪ X} = Umb(X) ∩ L. Here Umb(X) is the set of all elements ≪ X. This is the set of points of X.
- For a family F ⊂ M (for instance a figure F ∈ 𝓕), omb(F) = ∪_{X∈F} omb(X).
- The boundary is ∂X = X̃ \ {X}, where X̃ = {Y ∈ M | Y ≤ X} ∈ 𝓕 is the closure of X.
- The open shadow is omb(X)° = omb(X) − omb(∂X). These are the points of the 'open cell' X° = X \ ∂X. Write x ≪° X for x ∈ omb(X)°.

Step 3: the axiom MagL1.
- From axiom Mag 3: if X ∥ Y, then every point of X° is ∥ every point of Y°.
- He notes this is vacuous when omb(X)° or omb(Y)° is empty. He therefore imposes MagL1: for all X ∈ M, omb(X)° ≠ ∅. Every 'cell' has a point in its interior.
- In modern terms this is a non-degeneracy or 'spatiality' condition. It says the poset has enough points, like a CW or stratified complex in which every open stratum is non-empty.

Step 4: the realization map and the programme.
- MagL1 makes it possible to define the 'multi-shadow' maps M → Figel(L), X ↦ mulomb(X), and 𝓕 → Fig(L), F ↦ mulomb(F). These send elements and figures of the magasin to (elementary) figures on the set of points.
- He asks whether these maps are increasing for ≤ and ≪, and how they behave with the topological relations (≤, |∘|, ∥, …).
- He notes that the notions of homeomorphism and embedding for magasins (and later ateliers) must be revisited, citing earlier chapters ('CF VII p. 54', 'CF VI').

Purpose. The next page continues the thread. Axiom MagL2 says |∘| on M is determined by ∥ on points. This leads to a 'Proposition – Solution': a 'strictly divisible' structure is equivalent to the data (≤, ≪) plus a symmetric, antireflexive relation ∥ on L satisfying an incidence condition. So this page is the set-up for reducing the separation structure of a magasin to a 'point-set' datum. It parallels passing from a locale or face poset to its points.
errors: No real mathematical error. The 'tautological' equivalence x∥y ⇔ x|∘|y on lieux depends on axioms not visible here (definitions on earlier pages); it is plausible but unverified from this page alone.
Notation hesitation: the text first writes 'omb(X)° = omb(X)' and crosses it out, then corrects it to omb(X) − omb(∂X).

ideas.what: Points ('lieux') as the ≪-minimal elements of an abstract poset-like structure of 'figures'.
ideas.modern_name: Points of a poset/locale; vertices or minimal cells of a cell complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Locale theory (Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone); face posets of regular CW complexes
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this axiomatics is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Shadow omb(X) and open shadow omb(X)° = omb(X) − omb(∂X), with ∂X = closure minus X.
ideas.modern_name: Open stratum or open cell of a stratified space / face poset; set of points of the interior of a cell
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); in combinatorics, cell posets

ideas.what: Axiom MagL1: every element has a non-empty open shadow (enough points in every open cell).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogue of the enough-points conditions for locales and topoi (Deligne, SGA 4)

ideas.what: Realization maps X ↦ mulomb(X), F ↦ mulomb(F) into figures on the point set, plus the question of monotonicity and compatibility with the relations; morphisms and embeddings of magasins/ateliers to be revisited.
ideas.modern_name: Point-set realization of an abstract combinatorial topology; spatialization functor

missed.claim: The page belongs to an unpublished axiomatic 'combinatorial analysis situs' ('magasins' and 'ateliers', with relations ≤, ≪, |∘|, ∥). It is a framework for tame topology in which open-cell points are recovered from the combinatorics. This page only sets up definitions and a non-degeneracy axiom, so nothing on it is individually new. The framework as a whole is not in the literature.
missed.quote: MagL1 ∀X∈M, omb(X)°≠∅ … Il faudra revoir la notion d'homéomorphisme et des plongements pour les magasins
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal and definable-set formalisms, exit-path / stratified-space combinatorics and point-free topology. This is Grothendieck's own attempt at the 'topologie modérée' foundations called for in the Esquisse.

missed.claim: Open question left on the page: is mulomb monotone for ≤ and ≪, and is it compatible with |∘| and ∥? It is paired with the need to define homeomorphisms and embeddings of magasins.
missed.quote: savoir si c'est croissant pour ≤, ≪, comment … aux relations topologiques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a functoriality and realization question for an abstract stratified structure. It is minor in isolation.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine definitions (points, shadows, open cells) and a non-degeneracy axiom in Grothendieck's unpublished magasin axiomatics. The interest lies in the framework as a whole, not in this page.
transcription_corrections: 'umb(X)', 'umb(F)', 'umb(∂X)', 'mulumb' should read 'omb(X)', 'omb(F)', 'omb(∂X)', 'mulomb' ('ombre' = shadow), consistent with the next page. 'Umb(X)' is likely 'Omb(X)' (capital).
'Figel(L)' is probably 'Fig el(L)' (elementary figures), parallel to Fig(L).
'x ≪° X' is written as x with a small ∘ over ≪.
In the line about relations, the struck-out insertion reads roughly 'aux figures topologiques' / 'compatible' with ∈, ≤, |∘|, ∥; the image shows '∈' above the list.
'(ou plus les ateliers, par la suite)' is plausibly the intended reading of 'par c suite'.
The page number in the lower-left margin is '15' (archive pagination); the '6' at the top is Grothendieck's own page number.
